findings.defect: Zero-effect/bypass gate matches import paths plus bare selector identifiers. It does not resolve objects, so stdlib effects reachable through allowlisted imports and non-Go package sources pass.
findings.counterexample: Non-test mutants that compile and leave TestRepositoryBoundaryAndZeroEffects exit 0: time.Since/time.Until (physical clock); ed "crypto/ed25519" alias + ed.NewKeyFromSeed + x509.CreateCertificate (private-key signing); (*x509.Certificate).Verify with zero VerifyOptions (time.Now + system roots); x509.SystemCertPool (OS file I/O); body-less func + zz_rv_amd64.s assembly. Controls time.Now, unaliased ed25519.NewKeyFromSeed and os import are detected.
findings.reachability: Gate defense-in-depth only; the actual de71 non-test source contains none of these.
findings.fix: Type-check the package and resolve every selector to its types.Object; allowlist the exact stdlib functions/methods used today (sha256.Sum256, hex.EncodeToString/DecodeString, json.Marshal/Valid, x509.ParseCertificate, Certificate.CheckSignatureFrom, utf8.ValidString, bytes.Equal, strings.*, time type/methods without Now/Since/Until/timers), independent of import alias; refuse any non-.go source (.s/.syso/.c/.h) and any body-less func in the package.

findings.defect: checkPolicyBindings does not require the two cohort members to be distinct; K1 NewVerifier refuses 'duplicate external Node scope' only later.
findings.counterexample: Crypto fixture policy with Members[1] = Members[0] (scope, leaf DER, CA DER) and Slot PC4: checkPolicyBindings => nil; the same policy at the K1 bridge => K1_VALIDATION_REFUSED.
findings.reachability: Unreachable (no policy is issued in this slice). A future factory relying on this check would issue an opaque policy for an invalid cohort whose every use fails with the K1 code instead of TRUST_UNKNOWN_OR_PIN_MISMATCH at load.
findings.fix: Refuse equal canonical member scopes and equal leaf DER/SPKI across PC2/PC4 with TRUST_UNKNOWN_OR_PIN_MISMATCH; add the negative test.

findings.defect: Only the selected Operations entry is validated before K1. A consistent three-way ID substitution (query + facts + a new Operations entry that reuses the original lease hash, original entry kept), or an extra entry reusing a lease hash, passes checkOriginalHistory. K1 then refuses, so the code is K1_VALIDATION_REFUSED instead of the grant's ORIGINAL_PLAN_OPERATION_MISMATCH before K1.
findings.counterexample: TestRV_A3_Selectors 'three-way-current(original kept)' and 'extra-unrelated-op': pure=nil, full=K1_VALIDATION_REFUSED. Fail closed; nothing accepted.
findings.reachability: Fail-closed, code-mapping only. A fully consistent forged archive also belongs to archive authentication, which is HOLD.
findings.fix: For every Operations entry require key == OperationID, non-empty migration ID, fence >= 1, valid lease hash and UTC acquired<expires. Refuse duplicate LeaseEnvelopeSHA256 across entries, because one signed HELD lease names one operationId. Return ORIGINAL_PLAN_OPERATION_MISMATCH. Do not require exactly one entry: the legitimate fixture history has 2 operations.

HistoryReport and &Refusal{} are caller-constructible plain values. No API consumes them as authority, and future consumers must not.
The SPIFFE URI derivation mirrors K1 native.go:109 byte for byte. No new ambiguity is introduced; any '/'-in-scope ambiguity is K1 baseline.
